records.name: PRISM Quartet
records.summary: A saxophone quartet that commissions and records new music, tours, and runs an education institute for composers and players.
records.what_you_do: Attend a concert (the Concerts page lists dates and cities), join the mailing list and tick the volunteer box on the form, or take part in PRISM Quartet Institute programs such as masterclasses, coaching, and composition workshops.

schedule.text: No regular weekly schedule. Concerts, residencies and Institute sessions are booked one at a time and listed on the Concerts and Residencies pages.

cost.text: Concert prices are not listed on the site. The Institute's mentorship program is free to the artists it serves, and no other program fees are listed.

first_step.how: Go to a concert on the Concerts page, or join the mailing list and tick the volunteer box on the sign-up form.
first_step.basis: Concerts are public and the mailing list form is open to anyone, but the site names no volunteer roles, so the ways to help are general.
first_step.what_to_expect: A PRISM concert is a performance by four saxophonists, sometimes with a guest musician such as a pianist. Programs mix classical and jazz music, and recent releases include spoken word. The Concerts page lists the date, city and venue for each show but does not give ticket prices, so check the Find Out More page for the event before you go.
first_visit_tips: Check the Find Out More link on the concert listing for the venue and any admission details.
Email info@prismquartet.com with questions, since the site does not list ticket prices.

records.notes: Schedule text corrected: tier 1 had dated concerts and a blog date there, which now sit only in last_sign_of_life. The Institute page does not say which programs take applications or what they cost, and two programs are marked post-pandemic only, so their current status is unknown. The Contact page lists a Philadelphia mailing address that is not recorded as a location because it is not a public meeting place. The Concerts page year for the late October Michigan dates was not confirmed, so no date from it is written.

records.name: Prismatic Arts Ensemble
records.summary: A Philadelphia classical music group that stages concerts with bold programming, immersive staging, and storytelling.
records.what_you_do: Buy a ticket to one of its shows or donate through its support page. The site does not list classes, auditions, volunteer roles or membership.

schedule.text: Shows come as separate productions with their own run of dates, posted on the Up Next page. There is no regular weekly schedule.

cost.text: Ticket prices are not shown on the pages we read, so check each show's ticket page. Donations are taken through a fiscal sponsor's page.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket for the next listed show through the ticket link on the Up Next page.
first_step.basis: Shows are ticketed and open to the public. The site lists no classes, auditions or volunteer roles, so attending a show is the one clear way in.
first_step.what_to_expect: Shows are staged, with singing and storytelling built around a theme or a story. The company aims to revive rare and underperformed classical works. The site does not say how long a show runs or what seats cost, so check each show's ticket page first.
first_visit_tips: Check the ticket page for the start time and venue, since the Up Next page does not show them.
Email prismaticensemble@gmail.com with questions, since the site lists no phone number.

records.notes: The Up Next page lists items from September 2025 through May 2026 plus the June 2026 cabaret, with no later dates. The page does not show today's date, so the newest listed date is used. Tier 1 had the cabaret date in schedule text; it now sits only in last_sign_of_life. The About page says the group began in 2020. No venues or ticket prices appear on the Up Next page.

records.name: Project 440
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs creative leadership and college and career programs for young people in Philadelphia. In its semester program, teams plan arts-focused service projects in their neighborhoods.
records.what_you_do: Young people apply to Doing Good, a semester program where teams plan an arts-focused service project, or to Instruments for Success, a fall program that helps high school seniors with college and career applications. Alumni and School District of Philadelphia students can also join the Youth Advocacy Council, which meets twice a month and pays a stipend.

schedule.text: Programs run one semester at a time at Temple University's Center City Campus. Doing Good meets Mondays and Thursdays, and Instruments for Success meets Mondays and Wednesdays, both from 4:30 to 6:30 pm.

locations.label: Temple University Center City Campus (program sessions)

cost.text: The site says SEPTA passes and meals are provided, and students who meet attendance and participation rules earn a stipend at the end of the semester. The program pages do not say in plain words whether there is a fee. The Youth Advocacy Council pays $10 an hour.

first_step.how: On the Doing Good page, click Apply for Doing Good and fill in the online form. Seniors can use the Instruments for Success form instead.
first_step.basis: You must apply through an online form before you can take part. Doing Good is limited to 30 students per semester, and the page does not say how students are chosen.
first_step.what_to_expect: Doing Good starts with a few weeks of skills such as budgeting, marketing and event planning. Teams then pitch an arts-focused service project to a panel of experts and receive up to $500 to carry it out. Sessions meet Monday and Thursday from 4:30 to 6:30 pm, and students who meet the attendance rules earn a stipend at the end of the semester.
first_visit_tips: Ask for a SEPTA pass if you need one, since the program provides them.
Meals are provided, according to the site.
Several SEPTA lines and buses stop within one block of the Temple campus at 1515 Market Street.
Send travel questions to Marcus Bryant at mbryant@project440.org.

records.notes: The program pages give no year for the fall dates (Doing Good Sept 14 to Dec 21, Instruments for Success Sept 23 to Nov 4). The flyer file names disagree (Fall-2026 and Spring-2026), and one homepage read mentions a 2026 Fall Semester, so no year is written and status stays probably_active. One homepage read said participation is free, but the program pages do not say so, so cost is written cautiously. The Youth Advocacy Council page gives no meeting place or days. Partner names on the site (Philadelphia Music Alliance for Youth, Manhattan School of Music Scholarship) have no URL on the site, so they are not added as leads.

records.name: Project Capoeira, Inc.
records.summary: A nonprofit that teaches capoeira, a Brazilian style that blends fighting moves, music, dance and acrobatics, to people of all levels. It also runs kids classes, arts programs in schools and libraries, and public events such as Brazilian Day Philadelphia.
records.what_you_do: Take a weekly class at the Race Street studio: all-levels classes on weeknights, or Saturday classes split by age for kids from age 4 and up. Private lessons, workshops and performances can be booked, and donations are accepted. The site lists no volunteer or membership programs.

schedule.text: Weekly classes at the Race Street studio. Monday and Wednesday from 6:30 to 8 pm and Tuesday and Thursday from 6 to 7:30 pm are all-levels classes. Friday from 6:30 to 8 pm is open gym, kicks and roda (the playing circle). Saturday classes are split by age: ages 4 to 6 from 12:20 to 1 pm, ages 7 to 12 from 1 to 2 pm, and all levels from 2 to 3:30 pm.

locations.label: ASCAB Capoeira studio (where the classes meet)

cost.text: The website does not list class tuition, party prices, performance fees or a first-class price. Private lessons are offered, and payment is taken by Venmo or Cash App.

first_step.how: Go to an all-levels class at 1213 Race Street (Tuesday or Thursday 6 to 7:30 pm, or Monday or Wednesday 6:30 to 8 pm), or use the contact form to ask about the Saturday kids class for ages 4 and up.
first_step.basis: Classes are listed as all levels, kids classes start at age 4, and the site has a contact form for questions. It does not say how to book a first class or what one costs.
first_step.what_to_expect: Classes are held in a studio on the ground floor at 1213 Race Street, and weeknight sessions run about 90 minutes. Expect a class built around capoeira's moves, music and play. The site does not say what a first class costs, so ask the studio before you come.
first_visit_tips: Call 215-601-9117 or use the contact form to ask about a first class and prices, since the site does not list them.
For kids, ask which Saturday group fits the child's age: 4 to 6, 7 to 12, or the all-levels class.
The studio is on the ground floor at 1213 Race Street.

records.notes: The site lists weekly class times but no prices, first-class terms or current dates. Its event dates are from 2024 or have no year (the September 7 batizado), so no event date is written. Friday is open gym and roda time, not a class. The kids class Facebook page linked from the site was not read, since Facebook is lead only.

records.name: Project HOME Music Production Class
records.summary: A free three-week class for adults at Project HOME's learning center in North Philadelphia. Students learn Logic Pro, a professional music recording program.
records.what_you_do: Attend afternoon sessions Monday to Thursday for about three weeks and learn to record and build music in the software. Apply first through the form on the program page.

schedule.text: A three-week class that meets Monday to Thursday, 12:30 to 2:30 pm. Each session's dates are posted on the program page.

locations.label: Honickman Learning Center Comcast Technology Labs

cost.text: Free. The program page says the class costs nothing.

first_step.how: Fill in the application form linked from the program page before the November 18, 2026 deadline, or text MAP to (484) 229-3482 with questions.
first_step.basis: The class is open to any adult, but you must apply through a form before it starts, so it is not a walk-in class.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sessions run Monday to Thursday from 12:30 to 2:30 pm for about three weeks in the Comcast Technology Labs at the Honickman Learning Center. You learn Logic Pro, a professional music recording program, and practice recording and building music in it. The class is free for adults.
first_visit_tips: Apply by Wednesday, November 18, 2026, using the form on the program page.
The center is near 23rd and Berks in North Philadelphia, according to the program page.
The program page does not list accessibility, elevator or transit details, so ask by text before you go if you need them.

records.notes: The event page URL says July 2026, but the page itself is for the November 2026 session. The adult education page lists an October 12, 2026 computer class, which is the newest dated evidence. The center page names no accessibility, elevator or SEPTA stop, so none is recorded. A second time (12:00 PM on November 18) appears on the event page without explanation, so it is not used.

records.name: PURR (Philadelphia Urgent Rescue and Relief)
records.summary: An all-volunteer cat rescue run on donations. It trims colonies of outdoor cats, takes in sick or unwanted cats, runs a sanctuary, and places cats through adoption and foster homes.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer with sanctuary care, trap-neuter-return work, or driving cats where they need to go. You can also foster a cat, or help at the PURR Cat Cafe in Bridesburg, where adoptable cats live while they wait for homes.

schedule.text: No regular volunteer meeting schedule is published. The PURR Cat Cafe is open noon to 6 pm on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays and Mondays. Tuesday to Thursday hours are not listed.

cost.text: Volunteering and fostering are unpaid. Cat cafe visits cost $15 for regular admission, $10 all day on Fridays, and half price on Mondays.

first_step.how: Join PURR's volunteer Facebook group to see the open roles, or fill in the PURR Volunteer Form, a Google form linked from the volunteer page.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page names two clear ways to start, says people of all skill and physical levels can help, and says the group always needs more volunteers.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteer jobs range from sanctuary care, such as cleaning, replacing supplies, trimming shrubs and playing with the cats, to trap-neuter-return trips and driving cats where they need to go. People of all skill and physical levels can help, according to the site. The volunteer page does not say what training is offered or what shifts look like, so ask in the volunteer Facebook group. Volunteering is unpaid.
first_visit_tips: Book a cafe visit ahead through the booking link on the cafe page. The page does not say whether walk-ins are welcome.
The cafe's front door is at the corner of Orthodox and Thompson Streets.
Street parking can be tight, but the site says spots are usually open near the cemetery on Thompson Street.
The cafe page does not describe wheelchair access or step-free entry, so ask before you visit if you need it.

records.notes: The volunteer page gives no training, minimum age, shift or response-time details. The cafe page gives no accessibility or SEPTA stop details. The Tuesday to Thursday cafe hours are not listed. Cafe admission is charged, so the cost level is low rather than free. The only year on the site is in the copyright footer, which is not used as evidence.

records.name: Putty Dance Project
records.summary: A husband and wife team, a dancer and a composer, who make new dance works about social issues, mixing live jazz, projections and jazz dance improvisation.
records.what_you_do: Come to a performance and stay for the open conversation with the artists afterward. The group also runs Free Form Body Motif workshops in its jazz dance improvisation method, and you can ask about the next one through the contact form.

first_step.how: Check the upcoming performances and workshops on the site, then send a message through the contact form, choosing Other, to ask when the next workshop or show is.
first_step.basis: The site listed no upcoming performances or workshops when we checked, and it does not say how to sign up for a workshop, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The group makes new dance works about social issues, with live jazz, projections and jazz improvisation. Performances are followed by an open conversation between the artists and the audience, so you may be invited into the discussion. Recent shows were presented by Philadelphia Dance Projects, and the site does not give run times or ticket prices.
first_visit_tips: Look for the presenter's ticket page for a show, since recent shows were sold through Philadelphia Dance Projects.
Call 267-713-9783 to ask about upcoming workshops. The site lists this number for bookings and publicity.
Plan to stay after the show, since the artists hold an open conversation with the audience.

records.notes: The group's own site has no dates, prices, workshop times, ages or registration steps for workshops. The site's performances section showed no events when checked. The April 30 to May 2, 2026 run of Dance Like It's 1829 on a Philadelphia Dance Projects ticket listing is the newest dated evidence, and it sets the status. A second ticket listing for February 24 and 25 gives no year, so it is not used. A 2023 Broad Street Review preview came up in search but is not used. The workshop series is not dated, so no schedule text is written.

notes: Deep pass on 7 groups: 25 fetches (of up to 42 allowed) and 1 WebSearch (cap reached). No rate limiting and no blocked pages. Tier 1 had dated events in schedule or cost text for PRISM Quartet, Prismatic Arts Ensemble and Project HOME, and those were moved out or removed. Partner or venue names without a URL were not added as leads: Philadelphia Music Alliance for Youth and Manhattan School of Music Scholarship (Project 440 site), Settlement Music School (PRISM Quartet concert venue), Philadelphia Dance Projects (Putty presenter). Process note: one call to a tool outside the allowed list (a session widget reader) was made in error. It returned nothing, was not used, and no data came from it.
